name: Codification level
description: Where a piece of legislation sits within a code. schema.org lets you nest one part inside another (hasPart) but never says what kind of part it is — this fills that gap. Legal systems use different tiers in different orders, so publish whatever tier your own code uses and rely on isPartOf to show the actual nesting, rather than assuming every code has the same depth.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Code
hasDefinedTerm.description: The whole body of law, consolidated into one code.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Title
hasDefinedTerm.description: A top-level grouping, common in US municipal codes.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Book
hasDefinedTerm.description: A top-level grouping, common in civil-law codes.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Part
hasDefinedTerm.description: A grouping below title or book.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Chapter
hasDefinedTerm.description: A grouping below division, or the top-level grouping where a code has no title or book.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Article
hasDefinedTerm.description: The main numbered unit in most civil-law systems.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Section
hasDefinedTerm.description: The main numbered unit in most common-law systems.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Paragraph
hasDefinedTerm.description: A grouping below subsection, usually the smallest numbered unit.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Schedule
hasDefinedTerm.description: Extra material at the end of a document that still carries legal force.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Annex
hasDefinedTerm.description: Extra material at the end of a document — the usual term in EU and civil-law drafting.
